title: If Statement
description: Light an LED only when a knob is turned past halfway — with if.

steps.clip: You need: an Arduino Uno and its USB cable, a breadboard, 1 × knob (10 kΩ potentiometer), 1 × 220 Ω resistor, 1 × LED, and some jumper wires.
Push the knob into the breadboard, each of its three legs in its own column.
hints: The two outer legs are for power; the middle leg gives the reading.
steps.goal: Put the knob on the breadboard.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's GND pin → the blue − row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. One outer leg of the knob → that same row.
steps.goal: Connect one outer leg to GND.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's 5V pin → the red + row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. The knob's other outer leg → that same row.
hints: Now the knob has 0 V at one end and 5 V at the other.
steps.goal: Connect the other outer leg to 5V.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the knob's middle leg to pin A0 on the Arduino.
hints: A0 is on the ANALOG IN side of the Arduino.
The middle leg's voltage follows the knob: 0 V to 5 V.
steps.goal: Connect the knob's middle leg to A0.

steps.clip: Push a 220 Ω resistor into the breadboard. Put its two legs in two different columns.
hints: A resistor works either way round.
It protects the LED — without it the LED can burn out.
steps.goal: Put the resistor for the LED on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Run a wire from one leg of the 220 Ω resistor to pin 13 on the Arduino.
hints: Put the wire in any hole in the same column as the leg.
Pin 13 is on the Arduino's row of numbered sockets.

steps.clip: Put the LED in: the long leg in the same column as the 220 Ω resistor's other leg, the short leg in the next column.
hints: The long leg is + (the anode). Backwards, the LED stays dark.
Legs in the same column are connected — no wire needed.
steps.goal: Connect the LED's long leg (+) to the resistor.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the LED's short leg to the blue − row.
hints: GND is the minus side of the circuit.
steps.goal: Connect the LED's short leg (−) to GND.

steps.clip: Copy the code into the Arduino IDE and click Upload. Turn the knob: once the reading passes 400 the LED turns on.
